in_text_mentions: Histopathological evaluation disclosed total exudative retinal detachment and disorganization of the anterior segment (Fig. 3). The subretinal fluid was composed of PAS-positive material, cholesterol clefts and lipid-laden macrophages (Fig. 4). Lipid deposition was also seen in the retina inducing granulomatous inflammation foreign-body type (Fig. 5). In addition to the other findings, the presence of telangiectasic retinal vessels (Fig. 6) confirmed the diagnosis of Coats' disease.
